IR.rationale: A widening 5Y-over-funds spread signals markets pricing faster US tightening. This raises the global discount rate and pulls capital out of emerging markets.

B.rationale: Strong EM sovereign bond returns with US credit spreads not widening describe easy external financing for EM borrowers. That supports EM equity valuations.

V.rationale: High implied volatility carries an elevated variance and equity risk premium. EM equities, as high-beta assets, tend to earn higher subsequent returns from such states.

AP.rationale: US returns lead other markets because information diffuses gradually. A strong US week that EM has not yet matched points to catch-up.

ST.rationale: Momentum losses typically occur in sharp rebounds of beaten-down, high-beta assets. These states are associated with subsequent risk-on returns.

FX.rationale: A weakening broad dollar with a strengthening commodity currency describes easing global dollar funding and risk-on flows. Both favour EM equities.

COM.rationale: Rising commodity prices improve terms of trade and earnings for the many commodity-exporting emerging markets.

MC.rationale: High financial stress raises required risk premia. That depresses prices now and implies higher expected returns afterwards.

ENDG.rationale: Country-level index returns show time-series momentum at weekly-to-quarterly horizons, partly offset by short-term reversal.

IR.rationale: Sudden repricing of the US rate path is a recurrent source of capital-flow shocks and turbulence in emerging markets.

B.rationale: Widening credit spreads together with EM bond losses signal tightening external financing. Such states typically precede elevated equity volatility.

V.rationale: Implied volatility contains forward-looking information on future realised variance beyond what past realised variance already captures.

AP.rationale: Leverage and volatility-feedback effects make negative returns raise future volatility more than positive ones.

ST.rationale: Momentum drawdowns occur in panicky, high-volatility market states that tend to persist.

FX.rationale: A strong dollar combined with yen strength signals safe-haven demand and carry unwinding. These are risk-off conditions that raise EM volatility.

COM.rationale: Commodity price slumps hit EM fiscal and external balances and tend to come with higher EM equity volatility.

MC.rationale: Financial stress indices aggregate funding and market strains that forecast subsequent market turbulence.

ENDG.rationale: Volatility clusters, so a high recent realised variance persists beyond its average predictive effect.

IR.rationale: Abrupt pricing of US tightening can trigger EM capital outflows and sharp equity declines.

B.rationale: Simultaneous credit widening and EM debt selling signal a deteriorating risk appetite. Such regimes raise crash risk.

V.rationale: High implied volatility widens the return distribution and raises the probability of left-tail outcomes.

AP.rationale: Joint weakness in US and EM equities marks a global sell-off. Such sell-offs are prone to continuation through deleveraging.

ST.rationale: Momentum drawdowns coincide with distressed, high-volatility markets in which extreme moves are more likely.

FX.rationale: Dollar strength with commodity-currency weakness signals tightening dollar funding and risk-off flows, which precede EM losses.

COM.rationale: Falling commodity prices worsen the outlook for commodity-dependent emerging markets.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions constrain leverage and liquidity, raising the likelihood of forced selling.

ENDG.rationale: Weak recent returns signal a stressed, high-volatility regime in which further large declines are more likely.

IR.rationale: Falling medium-term yields relative to policy rates signal an easier expected US policy path. That supports flows into EM assets.

B.rationale: Strong returns on both EM and US high-yield debt describe a broad risk-on credit rally. Such rallies tend to coincide with strong EM equity gains.

V.rationale: High volatility widens both tails, and the largest rebounds typically follow periods of fear.

AP.rationale: Strong US equity returns lead global markets and signal improving risk appetite.

ST.rationale: Momentum crashes occur in sharp rebounds of beaten-down high-beta assets, a state linked with large subsequent gains.

FX.rationale: A weak dollar with commodity-currency strength eases EM financing conditions and fuels risk-on rallies.

COM.rationale: Commodity rallies boost terms of trade and earnings in commodity-exporting emerging markets.

MC.rationale: Elevated stress implies high risk premia and depressed prices. From such levels, large relief rallies are more likely.

ENDG.rationale: Large rebounds cluster after weak returns, reflecting both volatility clustering and short-term reversal.
